expectation: Nuclear stain in a small subset of CD3+CD4+ regulatory T cells, scattered singly or in small clusters within CD4-rich lymphoid or lamina propria areas. It should be rare and sit on CD4+ cells, not on epithelium or tissue background.
observed: A shows diffuse haze that follows tissue density, tile-like background squares and round bright blobs. B and C show haze with no discrete nuclear cells. D is a uniform bright haze. E1 has faint grain, and in E3 the green puncta mostly sit beside the CD4 cells, with only a few white overlaps.
why: The signal is haze, tiles and debris-like blobs, with no nuclear subset in the right place and little co-localisation with CD4.
notes: Haze follows tissue density, and the bright round blobs and tiles look like artefacts. No crisp nuclear subset appears in B, C or D, and FOXP3 barely overlaps the CD4+ cells in E.
